How does the grape boycott model — using consumer choice as a political tool — relate to the broader concept of 'everyday politics' in social movement theory?
items.stemEs: El boicot a las uvas de la UFW de César Chavez tuvo éxito en parte porque movilizó la conciencia moral del consumidor de una manera que las huelgas laborales puras no podían. ¿Cómo se relaciona el modelo del boicot a las uvas — usando la elección del consumidor como herramienta política — con el concepto más amplio de 'política cotidiana' en la teoría del movimiento social?

choices.text: The grape boycott model was unique to the Chicano Movement and could not be replicated by other social movements because it depended on the specific visibility of agricultural products in supermarkets.
choices.textEs: El modelo del boicot a las uvas fue único para el Movimiento Chicano y no pudo ser replicado por otros movimientos sociales porque dependía de la visibilidad específica de los productos agrícolas en los supermercados.

choices.text: The grape boycott model demonstrates that consumer activism is always more effective than formal labor organizing because consumers have more collective power than workers in capitalist economies.
choices.textEs: El modelo del boicot a las uvas demuestra que el activismo del consumidor es siempre más efectivo que la organización laboral formal porque los consumidores tienen más poder colectivo que los trabajadores en las economías capitalistas.

choices.text: The boycott had no connection to everyday politics theory because it was organized by a formal union rather than emerging spontaneously from individual consumer choices.
choices.textEs: El boicot no tuvo ninguna conexión con la teoría de la política cotidiana porque fue organizado por un sindicato formal en lugar de surgir espontáneamente de las elecciones individuales del consumidor.

choices.text: The grape boycott illustrates 'everyday politics' by transforming ordinary consumer decisions into accessible political acts — making political participation available to millions who would never engage in formal protest but could choose not to buy grapes.
choices.textEs: El boicot a las uvas ilustra la 'política cotidiana' al transformar las decisiones ordinarias del consumidor en actos políticos accesibles — haciendo que la participación política esté disponible para millones que nunca participarían en protestas formales pero podrían elegir no comprar uvas.

items.explanation: The grape boycott transformed the supermarket into a political arena and the act of grocery shopping into a political choice — demonstrating that the ordinary daily decisions of consumption had political implications. This embodies the concept of 'everyday politics': the idea that political action is not confined to elections, legislation, and formal protest but can occur through the collective exercise of choices available to ordinary people in their daily lives. The boycott was effective precisely because it did not require people to engage in risky or costly political action — simply choosing not to buy grapes was accessible to millions who would never join a picket line. This made the boycott a template for subsequent consumer activism, linking market choices to social justice.
items.explanationEs: El boicot a las uvas transformó el supermercado en una arena política y el acto de hacer las compras en una elección política — demostrando que las decisiones diarias ordinarias de consumo tenían implicaciones políticas. Esto encarna el concepto de 'política cotidiana': la idea de que la acción política no se limita a las elecciones, la legislación y la protesta formal sino que puede ocurrir a través del ejercicio colectivo de las opciones disponibles para la gente ordinaria en su vida diaria. El boicot fue efectivo precisamente porque no requería que la gente participara en acción política riesgosa o costosa — simplemente elegir no comprar uvas era accesible para millones que nunca se unirían a un piquete. Esto hizo que el boicot fuera una plantilla para el activismo del consumidor posterior, vinculando las elecciones del mercado con la justicia social.

items.stem: The Feminist Movement's campaign for the Equal Rights Amendment (ERA) failed to achieve ratification by 1982 despite Congressional passage in 1972. Which of the following best explains the causal chain that led to the ERA's defeat?
items.stemEs: La campaña del Movimiento Feminista por la Enmienda de Derechos Iguales (ERA) no logró la ratificación para 1982 a pesar de la aprobación del Congreso en 1972. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones explica mejor la cadena causal que llevó a la derrota de la ERA?

choices.text: The ERA failed because the Supreme Court ruled that the ratification process had exceeded its constitutional time limit, making ratification legally impossible regardless of state action.
choices.textEs: La ERA fracasó porque la Corte Suprema dictaminó que el proceso de ratificación había superado su límite de tiempo constitucional, haciendo que la ratificación fuera legalmente imposible independientemente de la acción estatal.

choices.text: A counter-mobilization led by Phyllis Schlafly successfully reframed the ERA as a threat to traditional gender roles and women's existing protections, building a coalition that stalled ratification in enough states to defeat it.
choices.textEs: Una contra-movilización liderada por Phyllis Schlafly reenmarcó exitosamente la ERA como una amenaza para los roles de género tradicionales y las protecciones existentes de las mujeres, construyendo una coalición que estancó la ratificación en suficientes estados para derrotarla.

choices.text: The ERA failed because feminist organizations abandoned their campaign in 1974 to focus on the Supreme Court abortion rights case, diverting resources away from ratification efforts at a critical moment.
choices.textEs: La ERA fracasó porque las organizaciones feministas abandonaron su campaña en 1974 para enfocarse en el caso de derechos al aborto de la Corte Suprema, desviando recursos de los esfuerzos de ratificación en un momento crítico.

choices.text: The ERA failed because Congress refused to extend the ratification deadline past 1979, and the Constitution's amendment process required ratification within exactly seven years of Congressional passage.
choices.textEs: La ERA fracasó porque el Congreso se negó a extender el plazo de ratificación más allá de 1979, y el proceso de enmienda de la Constitución requería la ratificación dentro de exactamente siete años de la aprobación del Congreso.

items.explanation: The ERA's defeat resulted from a counter-mobilization led by Phyllis Schlafly and the STOP ERA movement, which effectively reframed the amendment from a guarantee of equal rights to a threat to traditional gender roles, women's existing 'protections' (like mandatory alimony and exemption from military draft), and potentially to unisex bathrooms and same-sex marriage. Schlafly's coalition combined social conservatives, religious traditionalists, and women who genuinely feared that formal legal equality would undermine social arrangements they depended on. By 1975 the ratification momentum had stalled, and several states rescinded their prior ratifications. This illustrates that constitutional change requires sustained supermajority support that can be blocked by an effective minority counter-movement that successfully reframes the issue.
items.explanationEs: La derrota de la ERA resultó de una contra-movilización liderada por Phyllis Schlafly y el movimiento STOP ERA, que efectivamente reenmarcó la enmienda de una garantía de igualdad de derechos a una amenaza para los roles de género tradicionales, las 'protecciones' existentes de las mujeres (como la pensión alimenticia obligatoria y la exención del reclutamiento militar) y potencialmente a los baños unisex y el matrimonio entre personas del mismo sexo. La coalición de Schlafly combinó conservadores sociales, tradicionalistas religiosos y mujeres que genuinamente temían que la igualdad legal formal socavaría los arreglos sociales de los que dependían. Para 1975 el impulso de ratificación se había estancado y varios estados rescindieron sus ratificaciones anteriores. Esto ilustra que el cambio constitucional requiere un apoyo de supermayoría sostenida que puede ser bloqueado por un movimiento de contra-movilización minoritario efectivo que reenmarque exitosamente el problema.

items.stem: Scholars have debated whether the AIM, Chicano, and Feminist movements of the late 1960s–1970s 'succeeded' or 'failed.' Which of the following provides the most analytically sophisticated framework for evaluating the outcomes of these movements?
items.stemEs: Los académicos han debatido si los movimientos AIM, Chicano y Feminista de finales de la década de 1960 a la de 1970 'tuvieron éxito' o 'fracasaron'. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones proporciona el marco analíticamente más sofisticado para evaluar los resultados de estos movimientos?

choices.text: Movement outcomes should be evaluated across multiple dimensions — policy, organizational, cultural, and structural — recognizing that movements can achieve significant changes along some dimensions while falling short on others, making binary success/failure judgments inadequate.
choices.textEs: Los resultados del movimiento deben evaluarse a través de múltiples dimensiones — política, organizativa, cultural y estructural — reconociendo que los movimientos pueden lograr cambios significativos en algunas dimensiones mientras se quedan cortos en otras, haciendo que los juicios binarios de éxito/fracaso sean inadecuados.

choices.text: The most appropriate framework is purely electoral: movements succeed if their demands are adopted as party platforms by major political parties and fail if they are not incorporated into electoral politics.
choices.textEs: El marco más apropiado es puramente electoral: los movimientos tienen éxito si sus demandas son adoptadas como plataformas de partido por los principales partidos políticos y fracasan si no se incorporan a la política electoral.

choices.text: Movement success should be measured solely by whether the movement's specific legislative demands were enacted into law, since only statutory change produces durable social transformation.
choices.textEs: El éxito del movimiento debe medirse únicamente por si las demandas legislativas específicas del movimiento fueron promulgadas como ley, ya que solo el cambio estatutario produce una transformación social duradera.

choices.text: The most accurate framework is structural: movements succeed only when they achieve measurable reductions in economic inequality between groups, since all other changes are merely symbolic without material impact.
choices.textEs: El marco más preciso es estructural: los movimientos tienen éxito solo cuando logran reducciones medibles en la desigualdad económica entre grupos, ya que todos los demás cambios son meramente simbólicos sin impacto material.

items.explanation: Evaluating social movement outcomes requires distinguishing among different types of change they sought and achieved: policy outcomes (specific laws or court rulings), organizational outcomes (new institutions, representation), cultural outcomes (changed norms, language, consciousness), and structural outcomes (reduced inequality). Each movement achieved significant cultural and institutional changes (women's studies programs, tribal colleges, bilingual education, women's entry into professions, changed gender norms) while falling short of structural goals (ongoing poverty, continuing treaty violations, persistent gender wage gaps). The question of 'success' or 'failure' thus requires specifying: compared to what baseline, along what dimensions, over what time frame? A binary success/failure framework obscures the partial, uneven, and continuing nature of social movement outcomes.
items.explanationEs: Evaluar los resultados de los movimientos sociales requiere distinguir entre los diferentes tipos de cambio que buscaron y lograron: resultados de políticas (leyes o fallos judiciales específicos), resultados organizativos (nuevas instituciones, representación), resultados culturales (normas cambiadas, lenguaje, conciencia) y resultados estructurales (desigualdad reducida). Cada movimiento logró cambios culturales e institucionales significativos (programas de estudios de la mujer, universidades tribales, educación bilingüe, entrada de mujeres a las profesiones, normas de género cambiadas) mientras se quedaba corto en los objetivos estructurales (pobreza continua, violaciones continuas de los tratados, brechas salariales de género persistentes). La pregunta de 'éxito' o 'fracaso' requiere especificar: en comparación con qué línea de base, a lo largo de qué dimensiones, en qué plazo de tiempo. Un marco binario de éxito/fracaso oscurece la naturaleza parcial, desigual y continua de los resultados de los movimientos sociales.

items.stem: The Feminist, Chicano, and AIM movements all emerged during a period of broader social upheaval (1965–1975) that also included the anti-Vietnam War movement and the counterculture. A historian argues that these movements were not separate phenomena but expressions of a single crisis of legitimacy in American institutions. Which of the following best evaluates this interpretive claim?
items.stemEs: Los movimientos Feminista, Chicano y AIM surgieron todos durante un período de agitación social más amplia (1965–1975) que también incluyó el movimiento contra la Guerra de Vietnam y la contracultura. Un historiador argumenta que estos movimientos no eran fenómenos separados sino expresiones de una sola crisis de legitimidad en las instituciones estadounidenses. ¿Cuál de las siguientes opciones evalúa mejor esta afirmación interpretativa?

choices.text: The 'single crisis' interpretation is fully accurate: all social movements of the 1965–1975 period were expressions of the same Marxist class consciousness that unified them as a single revolutionary movement against capitalism.
choices.textEs: La interpretación de 'crisis única' es completamente precisa: todos los movimientos sociales del período 1965–1975 fueron expresiones de la misma conciencia de clase marxista que los unificó como un único movimiento revolucionario contra el capitalismo.

choices.text: The 'single crisis' interpretation is entirely wrong: each movement operated in complete isolation with no awareness of or influence from other contemporary movements.
choices.textEs: La interpretación de 'crisis única' es completamente incorrecta: cada movimiento operó en completo aislamiento sin ningún conocimiento o influencia de otros movimientos contemporáneos.

choices.text: The interpretation captures real commonalities of era and cross-pollination among movements but risks obscuring the distinct community-specific conditions and demands that gave each movement its particular historical character and political logic.
choices.textEs: La interpretación captura similitudes reales de la era y polinización cruzada entre movimientos, pero arriesga oscurecer las condiciones específicas de la comunidad y las demandas distintas que le dieron a cada movimiento su carácter histórico particular y lógica política.

choices.text: The 'crisis of legitimacy' framework is only applicable to the Black civil rights movement; the other movements emerged from fundamentally different causes unrelated to institutional legitimacy questions.
choices.textEs: El marco de 'crisis de legitimidad' solo es aplicable al movimiento de derechos civiles negro; los otros movimientos surgieron de causas fundamentalmente diferentes no relacionadas con preguntas de legitimidad institucional.

items.explanation: The 'crisis of legitimacy' interpretation has analytical merit: the Vietnam War, urban uprisings, political assassinations, and civil rights failures all contributed to a broad questioning of American institutions' claims to represent democratic values. The movements shared a common critique of existing power structures and drew inspiration from each other. However, the unifying framework can obscure important differences: each movement arose from distinct community-specific conditions (reservation poverty and treaty violations for AIM; agricultural labor exploitation for Chicanos; domestic and professional exclusion for women) that required different analyses and different demands. The interpretation captures real commonalities of era and cross-pollination while risking reduction of distinct political projects to a single narrative that flattens their specific historical contexts.
items.explanationEs: La interpretación de la 'crisis de legitimidad' tiene mérito analítico: la Guerra de Vietnam, los levantamientos urbanos, los asesinatos políticos y los fracasos de los derechos civiles contribuyeron todos a un amplio cuestionamiento de las afirmaciones de las instituciones estadounidenses de representar los valores democráticos. Los movimientos compartieron una crítica común de las estructuras de poder existentes y se inspiraron mutuamente. Sin embargo, el marco unificador puede oscurecer diferencias importantes: cada movimiento surgió de condiciones específicas de la comunidad (pobreza en las reservas y violaciones de los tratados para AIM; explotación del trabajo agrícola para los chicanos; exclusión doméstica y profesional para las mujeres) que requerían diferentes análisis y diferentes demandas. La interpretación captura similitudes reales de la era y polinización cruzada mientras arriesga reducir proyectos políticos distintos a una narrativa única que aplana sus contextos históricos específicos.

items.stem: Barack Obama was elected president in 2008, becoming the first African American to hold the office, in an election in which his campaign's digital organizing and social media strategy played significant roles. How should Obama's 2008 election be evaluated in terms of what it does and does not represent about the state of racial equality and democratic participation in the United States?

choices.text: Obama's election demonstrated that the United States had achieved a post-racial society in which individual merit, effective campaigning, and strong policy positions could overcome racial barriers in national electoral competition, vindicating the optimistic reading of the progress American democracy had made since the civil rights era.

Obama's electoral victory was produced primarily by exceptional economic crisis conditions — the 2008 financial collapse — that would have produced a Democratic victory for virtually any candidate, meaning the racial significance of his election was secondary to the economic cycle that drove the fundamental electoral dynamic of the year.

Obama's election represented a historic milestone in African American political achievement, but it cannot be interpreted as evidence of structural racial equality since persistent racial gaps in wealth, educational opportunity, criminal justice outcomes, and political representation continued largely unchanged by the election of a single Black president.

The election's most historically significant aspect was the transformation of digital and social media organizing into presidential campaign infrastructure, as the demographic mobilization of young and minority voters that Obama's campaign achieved through these tools fundamentally restructured the electoral coalition possibilities for the Democratic Party going forward.

items.explanation: Obama's election was simultaneously historically significant as an achievement and analytically insufficient as evidence of structural equality: the same election cycle produced documented evidence of racial voting patterns in certain regions, and the structural conditions that produce racial inequality — wealth gaps, incarceration rates, educational disparities — were unaffected by the executive branch transition. items.stem: Which best explains how the 2008 financial crisis revealed a fundamental structural weakness in the American financial system?

choices.text: Financial institutions had invested heavily in foreign currency markets without adequate hedging, exposing American banks to international exchange rate volatility.
The Federal Reserve's decision to raise interest rates in 2006–2007 triggered mortgage defaults that financial institutions' risk models had failed to anticipate.

The repeal of Glass-Steagall regulations allowed commercial and investment banking to merge, creating institutions whose interconnected exposure to mortgage-backed securities made their failure impossible to contain.
The subprime mortgage crisis was primarily the result of widespread fraud by individual borrowers rather than structural incentives within the lending and securitization industry.

items.explanation: The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (1999) repealed Glass-Steagall's separation of commercial and investment banking. The resulting 'too big to fail' institutions created and traded in mortgage-backed securities that spread housing market risk throughout the entire financial system — so that when the housing bubble burst, the failure of a few institutions threatened the entire economy.

Evaluate the significance of the farmworkers' movement led by Cesar Chavez within the larger context of social movements of the 1960s and 1970s.
items.stemEs: Evalúe la importancia del movimiento de trabajadores agrícolas dentro del contexto más amplio de los movimientos sociales de los años 1960 y 1970.

choices.text: The farmworkers' movement was isolated from other social movements and had no broader significance
Chavez's movement achieved all its goals immediately and permanently ended exploitation of farmworkers

The movement expanded the definition of civil rights beyond racial equality to include economic justice and Latino rights, while demonstrating that marginalized groups could organize effectively using nonviolent collective action
The farmworkers' movement only affected California and had no national impact

items.explanation: Chavez's movement was transformative on multiple levels: it won concrete gains (union contracts, banning of dangerous pesticides); expanded civil rights discourse to include economic justice and Latino identity; built a model of multiracial coalition (Filipino and Mexican workers); and inspired subsequent movements for immigrant rights. The grape boycott became one of the most successful consumer boycotts in American history.
items.explanationEs: El movimiento expandió la definición de derechos civiles para incluir justicia económica y derechos latinos.

Analyze the ERA debate as a reflection of the broader cultural tensions in American society during the 1970s.
items.stemEs: Analice el debate sobre la ERA como reflejo de las tensiones culturales más amplias en la sociedad estadounidense de los años 1970.

choices.text: The ERA debate was a minor issue that attracted little public attention or controversy
Both supporters and opponents of the ERA agreed on the role of women in society but disagreed only on legal technicalities
The ERA debate was limited to women and did not involve men or broader political movements

The ERA fight reflected a deepening divide between the feminist movement seeking legal equality and a rising conservative movement defending traditional gender roles, foreshadowing the culture wars of subsequent decades

items.explanation: The ERA debate crystallized a fundamental cultural divide: feminists saw it as essential to legal equality, while social conservatives viewed it as an attack on the family and traditional values. The anti-ERA movement helped build the New Right coalition that elected Ronald Reagan in 1980, connecting opposition to feminism with broader conservative causes like opposition to abortion, gun control, and big government.
items.explanationEs: El debate de la ERA reflejó una división profunda entre el movimiento feminista y un movimiento conservador en ascenso.

Evaluate the long-term impact of the American Indian Movement on federal policies toward Native Americans.
items.stemEs: Evalúe el impacto a largo plazo del Movimiento Indígena Americano en las políticas federales hacia los nativos americanos.

choices.text: AIM had no lasting impact and federal policies toward Native Americans remained unchanged
AIM raised national awareness and contributed to policy changes including the Indian Self-Determination Act (1975) and the return of tribal lands, though many fundamental issues remain unresolved
AIM achieved all its goals and fully resolved the issues of Native American poverty, health, and sovereignty
AIM's confrontational tactics permanently damaged the relationship between Native Americans and the federal government

items.explanation: AIM's activism contributed to significant policy shifts: the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (1975) gave tribes greater control over federal programs; the American Indian Religious Freedom Act (1978) protected sacred practices; and several land claims were settled. However, poverty, health disparities, and sovereignty issues persist on many reservations, indicating that AIM's goals remain partially unfulfilled.
items.explanationEs: AIM contribuyó a cambios de política significativos, pero muchos problemas fundamentales permanecen sin resolver.
